focal_region.annotated_sentence_text:
[Turn 1 USER]
e001	I run a local nonprofit newsroom with eleven full-time staff.
e002	A large neighborhood platform has offered to feature our reporting in a dedicated local-news section and share advertising revenue.
e003	Their reach could materially increase our audience, and the money could fund a second city-hall reporter.
e004	I am excited by that possibility but worried that we will start shaping coverage around what performs inside their feed.
e005	I cannot tell whether my hesitation protects editorial independence or protects an old idea that serious journalism must struggle to remain serious.
[Turn 1 ASSISTANT]
e006	The offer combines reach, revenue, public-service impact, and dependence on someone else's distribution rules.
e007	Those benefits can be real even if the platform's incentives later narrow what gets seen.
e008	Separate what the contract controls from what the ranking system controls and from habits your own newsroom may adopt without being asked.
e009	Your concern about identity should not erase the operating risk, but the operating risk should not become a reason to romanticize limited reach.
[Turn 7 USER]
e049	I am leaning toward a four-month nonexclusive pilot limited to service and explanatory stories, with our approval of every feed headline, story-level distribution and correction logs, and no homepage widget.
e050	I will tell the board we should describe it as a distribution test, not an institutional endorsement, and that investigations remain outside the evidence it can produce.
e051	I am willing to allow a widget only on participating stories and to stop the pilot if correction delays or unexplained ranking changes cross thresholds we set before launch.
e052	I have not resolved how much staff adaptation during the pilot would count as useful learning versus quiet self-censorship.
[Turn 7 ASSISTANT]
e053	The position separates a bounded distribution experiment from endorsement and from a broader channel strategy.
e054	Headline approval, story-level logs, correction thresholds, and the homepage boundary make the test more observable without making it neutral.
e055	The pilot cannot show how the platform would handle investigations, and staff may change story choices in anticipation of platform performance even without an explicit request.
e056	Ending the pilot also cannot fully reverse audience habits, donor expectations, or source perceptions created while it runs.

question: What starting position, attraction, hesitation, or undecided stance is visible before the current position? Do not infer a start that the source does not show.
